integrity: The proof is symbolic. It independently checks that the idealization is local non-strong phi-Pruefer, identifies its canonical kernel, computes Tor_1^D(Q/D,Q/D) from a two-term flat resolution, and then applies the published canonical-kernel recurrence plus exact-sequence dimension shifting. No finite experiment is used as evidence for an infinite statement.
scientific_limitations: The exact module stabilization uses the special divisible torsion module Q/D and is not asserted for arbitrary canonical kernels of non-strong phi-Pruefer rings. No finite-generation or minimal-free-resolution statement is made.
title: Exact parity Tor algebra for valuation idealizations by the fraction quotient
